questions.q: In a Kubernetes rolling update with `maxUnavailable: 1` and 6 replicas, what is guaranteed during the rollout?
options: At least 5 pods remain healthy and serving traffic at all times
All 6 pods are taken down simultaneously and replaced at once
Only the new version serves traffic from the first moment
No pods are available until the rollout fully completes
questions.explain: maxUnavailable: 1 caps how many pods can be down at once, so with 6 replicas Kubernetes never drops below 5 healthy pods during the update.

questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a blue-green deployment?
options: Traffic gradually shifts between old and new versions over several hours
Two complete environments run side by side, and all traffic switches from one to the other in a single atomic cutover
Only 10% of pods ever run the new version
The old version is deleted before the new version is deployed
questions.explain: Blue-green keeps two full environments and flips all traffic at once, avoiding any in-between state where both versions serve traffic simultaneously.

questions.q: What problem is canary deployment specifically good at catching?
options: Syntax errors in a Dockerfile
Problems that only show up under real production traffic or real user behavior, which a staging environment didn't reproduce
Missing unit tests in a pull request
Whether a container image was tagged correctly
questions.explain: By sending a small slice of real traffic to the new version, canary deployment can surface issues tied to real-world conditions that staging, however realistic, didn't actually trigger.

questions.q: Why might Northbridge Retail choose blue-green specifically for a database schema change rather than a rolling update?
options: Blue-green is always faster to execute than a rolling update
A rolling update briefly runs old and new versions side by side, which is unacceptable when even brief version mixing against a changed schema could cause data problems
Rolling updates are not supported by Kubernetes for schema changes
Blue-green requires fewer total servers than a rolling update
questions.explain: Blue-green avoids any period where old and new code run simultaneously, which matters most when the two versions aren't safely compatible with the same data, as with schema changes.

questions.q: What does 'blast radius' mean in the context of choosing a deployment strategy?
options: The physical size of the data center running the deployment
How much of real traffic or how many real users are exposed if the new version turns out to be broken
The number of container images produced by a single build
The total time a deployment takes to complete
questions.explain: Blast radius describes the scope of exposure to a potential problem — canary deployment deliberately keeps this small by only routing a fraction of traffic to the new version at first.
